requirements.requirement: curl's currently installed version is locked/held on node1 so a system update will not change it
requirements.summary: python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock was installed and 'dnf versionlock add curl' created a lock entry curl-0:7.76.1-40.el9.*, confirmed present both immediately after application and again after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: The lock actually prevents curl from being upgraded during a system update
requirements.summary: A newer curl-7.76.1-40.el9_8.7 was confirmed available in the repo, yet 'dnf check-update curl' reported no update, and a real 'dnf upgrade --assumeno' dry-run against the full 98-package update set (verified via a targeted grep) upgraded libcurl but excluded curl itself, both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered state, for every managed node (node1)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id bf4e9cbb-... and healthy curl/lock state were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, node1 was unreachable during the transition, a new boot_id aca0026b-... with ~25s uptime was observed post-restart, and curl package/lock/upgrade-exclusion state was re-verified as recovered. This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare bf4e9cbb-... vs after_executor aca0026b-...) and by no failed services/package-health regressions in the lifecycle comparison.

overall_summary: The executor correctly applied and verified a dnf versionlock hold on curl's installed version (7.76.1-40.el9) on node1, demonstrated with a concrete newer version available in the repo that the hold excludes curl from both check-update and a real dry-run upgrade of 98 packages, and additionally ran the required node-restart evidence protocol showing a full reboot (boot_id change, brief unreachability, low post-restart uptime) with the lock and curl version confirmed intact afterward. All observed mutations were purposeful and low-risk; only a minor leftover /tmp/reboot.log was not cleaned up.
limitations: No independent read-only confirmation of the versionlock config file contents (e.g., /etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.d/curl.list) beyond the 'dnf versionlock list' CLI output was captured.

The dry-run upgrade evidence relies on --assumeno output rather than an actual completed system update, though this is a reasonable and standard way to prove the hold without risking an unwanted real upgrade.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (versionlock plugin install, versionlock add, systemctl reboot) map directly to satisfying the task, verifying the hold, or executing the mandated restart evidence protocol. The dnf upgrade commands used --assumeno and aborted, causing no package changes. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file created by the nohup-backgrounded reboot command and left in place post-restart (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot); this is a low-risk, expected byproduct of triggering a reboot over a disconnecting exec channel rather than an unnecessary or destructive mutation, but it was not cleaned up.
